PROTECT YOURSELF ONLINE
Scammers are becoming increasingly sophisticated, and anyone can (1) ______ victim to their tricks. Follow these simple guidelines to keep your personal information safe.

questions.q: Choose the option that best fits blank (2).
questions.e: 'however + adj + S + may seem' = dù có … đến đâu. 'whatever' đi với danh từ; 'no matter' phải kèm 'how' (no matter how urgent); 'although' không đứng trước tính từ theo cấu trúc này.

questions.q:
Choose the correct arrangement of the following exchanges to make a meaningful conversation.
a. Linh: Not really. I was hoping you could give me a hand with the slides.
b. Khoa: Have you finished preparing for tomorrow's presentation?
c. Khoa: Sure, I'm free after lunch. Let's meet in the library.
questions.e: Khoa hỏi (b) → Linh trả lời 'Not really' và nhờ giúp (a) → Khoa đồng ý, hẹn gặp (c).

questions.q:
Choose the correct arrangement of the following exchanges to make a meaningful conversation.
a. Mai: That sounds ideal. Is there an entrance fee?
b. Tuan: There's a new art exhibition at the museum this weekend. Would you like to go?
c. Tuan: No, it's free for students, but we need to book a time slot online.
d. Mai: I'd love to! What kind of art is it?
e. Tuan: Mostly contemporary paintings by young Vietnamese artists.
questions.e: Lời mời (b) → nhận lời, hỏi loại tranh (d) → trả lời (e) → 'That sounds ideal', hỏi phí vào cửa (a) → 'No, it's free…' (c).

questions.q:
Choose the correct arrangement of the sentences to make a meaningful letter.
a. Unfortunately, when the package arrived, two of the four items were missing.
b. I am writing to express my dissatisfaction with an order I placed on your website on 3 March.
c. I would therefore be grateful if you could send the missing items or issue a full refund within fourteen days.
d. When I contacted your customer service team, I was told that the problem would be resolved within 48 hours, but I have heard nothing since.
e. I have attached a copy of my receipt for your reference.
Dear Sir or Madam,
questions.e: Nêu mục đích thư (b) → sự cố thiếu hàng (a) → đã liên hệ nhưng không được giải quyết (d) → 'therefore' đề nghị gửi hàng/ hoàn tiền (c) → đính kèm hóa đơn (e).

questions.q:
Choose the correct arrangement of the sentences to make a meaningful paragraph.
a. This is because switching between languages requires the brain to constantly select one system while suppressing the other.
b. Speaking two languages is often seen mainly as a practical skill for travel or work.
c. Over time, this mental exercise may strengthen abilities such as attention control and multitasking.
d. However, a growing body of research suggests that bilingualism may also shape the way the brain functions.
e. Even so, scientists continue to debate how large and long-lasting these advantages really are.
questions.e: Quan niệm phổ biến (b) → 'However' quan điểm mới (d) → 'This is because' giải thích (a) → 'this mental exercise' (= việc chuyển đổi ngôn ngữ ở a) (c) → 'Even so… these advantages' (e).

questions.q:
Choose the correct arrangement of the sentences to make a meaningful paragraph.
a. What mattered instead was a shared sense among members that they could speak up without fear of embarrassment.
b. When analysing the data, the researchers expected the best-performing groups to be those with the most talented individuals.
c. A team of organisational psychologists once set out to discover what makes some work groups more effective than others.
d. To their surprise, however, the level of individual talent made little difference.
e. This finding has since encouraged many managers to focus less on hiring stars and more on building trust.
questions.e: Giới thiệu nghiên cứu (c) → giả thuyết ban đầu (b) → 'To their surprise, however' tài năng cá nhân không quan trọng (d) → 'What mattered instead' – yếu tố thực sự quan trọng (a) → ứng dụng 'This finding' (e). 'instead' ở a cần câu phủ định d đứng trước.

questions.q: Choose the option that best fits blank (1).
o: to whom local people and customs are known along the way
which getting to know local people and customs along the way
got to know local people and customs along the way
getting to know local people and customs along the way
questions.e: Cụm V-ing chỉ hành động đi kèm, cùng chủ ngữ 'slow travellers': ở lâu hơn, qua đó làm quen người dân và phong tục. 'got' sai thì và thiếu liên từ; 'which getting' sai cấu trúc; 'to whom… are known' sai nghĩa.
questions.ctx:
Read the following passage and choose the option that best fits each numbered blank.

Slow travel is a way of exploring the world that values depth over speed. Rather than rushing to see as many famous sights as possible, slow travellers choose to stay longer in fewer places, (1) ______.
The movement grew partly out of frustration with the pressures of modern tourism. Many visitors return home from packed itineraries feeling more exhausted than refreshed, (2) ______. Slow travel offers an alternative: travelling by train or bus instead of by plane, cooking with local ingredients, and spending time in neighbourhoods (3) ______.
Supporters also point to its environmental advantages. (4) ______, slow travellers typically produce fewer carbon emissions than those who hop between destinations by air.
Of course, slow travel is not an option for everyone. It requires time, (5) ______, and many workers simply cannot take several weeks off. Still, even within a short holiday, the principle of doing less but experiencing more can be applied.

questions.q: Choose the option that best fits blank (2).
o: as if they needed another holiday to recover from the first
which they needed another holiday to recover from the first
as though needed another holiday to recover from the first
so needing another holiday to recover from the first
questions.e: 'as if + S + V (quá khứ)' = như thể họ cần thêm một kỳ nghỉ để hồi phục sau kỳ nghỉ đầu – hợp ý 'mệt hơn là khỏe'. 'as though needed' thiếu chủ ngữ; 'so needing' sai cấu trúc; 'which they needed… from the first' thừa tân ngữ.

questions.q: Not until she read the letter a second time ______ how serious the situation was.
questions.e: Đảo ngữ với 'Not until + mốc/ mệnh đề': đảo ở mệnh đề chính → 'did she realise'.

questions.q: The committee has decided to ______ the final decision until more evidence is available.
questions.e: 'put off' = trì hoãn, hợp với 'until more evidence is available'. 'put up' = dựng/ cho ở nhờ, 'put out' = dập tắt, 'put down' = đặt xuống/ ghi lại.

questions.q: Had the warning been taken seriously, the damage ______.
questions.e: Đảo ngữ điều kiện loại 3 (Had + S + V3) → mệnh đề chính 'could/ would have + V3'; 'damage' chịu tác động nên dùng bị động 'could have been avoided'.

questions.q: Her latest novel has received ______ reviews from critics across the country.
questions.e: Collocation 'glowing reviews' = những lời nhận xét hết sức khen ngợi. Các tính từ còn lại không kết hợp với 'reviews'.

questions.t: Ngữ pháp – mệnh đề quan hệ
questions.q: The manager, ______ advice the whole team had always relied, announced her retirement yesterday.
questions.e: 'rely on sb's advice' → giới từ 'on' đưa lên trước đại từ quan hệ sở hữu: 'on whose advice the team had relied'. 'on whom' không đi kèm danh từ 'advice'; 'of which' dùng cho vật.

questions.q:
Where in paragraph 1 does the following sentence best fit?
'Delaying the task brings immediate, if temporary, relief from these emotions.'
questions.e: Câu chèn có 'these emotions' → phải đứng sau câu liệt kê cảm xúc (boredom, anxiety, self-doubt); câu ngay sau nó 'Unfortunately, this relief is short-lived' cần 'relief' ở câu trước → vị trí [III].
questions.ctx:
Almost everyone has, at some point, postponed an important task in favour of something more pleasant. [I] Procrastination is commonly regarded as a problem of poor time management, but psychologists increasingly see it in a different light. [II] In their view, people put off tasks not because they cannot plan their time, but because the tasks themselves trigger unpleasant feelings such as boredom, anxiety or self-doubt. [III] Unfortunately, this relief is short-lived, and the task usually becomes even more stressful as the deadline approaches. [IV]
This emotional explanation helps to account for a puzzling feature of procrastination: it is often most severe among people who care deeply about the outcome. A student who fears that an essay will not be good enough may find it easier to avoid starting altogether than to confront the possibility of failure. In this sense, procrastination can act as a kind of shield, protecting a person's self-image in the short term while damaging their performance in the long term.
If procrastination is rooted in emotion, then strategies that focus only on schedules and to-do lists are unlikely to be enough. Experts instead recommend approaches that make the first step less threatening. Breaking a large project into small, concrete actions, for example, reduces the sense of being overwhelmed. Some people also find it helpful to commit to working on a task for just five minutes; once they have started, continuing is often far easier than they expected.
Perhaps most importantly, researchers suggest treating oneself with understanding rather than harsh criticism after a lapse. Self-blame may seem like a way to stay motivated, but it tends to intensify the negative feelings that caused the delay in the first place.

questions.q: The word 'short-lived' in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.e: 'short-lived' = tồn tại trong thời gian ngắn → 'brief'.

o: Because the deadline is still far away
To avoid facing the possibility that the essay will not be good enough

To have more time for planning a better schedule
questions.e: Đoạn 2: học sinh sợ bài luận không đủ tốt nên né việc bắt đầu thay vì 'confront the possibility of failure'.

If procrastination is rooted in emotion, then strategies that focus only on schedules and to-do lists are unlikely to be enough. Experts instead recommend approaches that make the first step less threatening. Breaking a large project into small, concrete actions, for example, reduces the sense of being overwhelmed. Some people also find it helpful to commit to working on a task for just five minutes; once they have started, continuing is often far easier than they expected.
Perhaps most importantly, researchers suggest treating oneself with understanding rather than harsh criticism after a lapse. Self-blame may seem like a way to stay motivated, but it tends to intensify the negative feelings that caused the delay in the first place.

questions.q: Which of the following could be the best title for the passage?
o: Silent Losses: Why Languages Die and How They Can Be Saved
Why Linguists Have Stopped Studying Small Languages
The Extinction of Plant and Animal Species
How Global Languages Improve Children's Opportunities
questions.e: Bài nêu hiện trạng ngôn ngữ biến mất, nguyên nhân (đoạn 2), tầm quan trọng (đoạn 3) và nỗ lực phục hồi (đoạn 4) → 'Silent Losses: Why Languages Die and How They Can Be Saved' bao quát nhất.
questions.ctx:
Of the thousands of languages spoken in the world today, a large proportion are used by only a small number of people, and many linguists fear that a significant share of them could fall silent by the end of this century. Unlike the extinction of a plant or animal species, the death of a language rarely makes headlines. Yet when the last fluent speaker of a language passes away, a unique way of understanding the world may disappear with them.
Languages seldom vanish because their speakers are forbidden to use them, although this has happened. More often, the process is gradual and almost invisible. Parents who believe that a dominant national or global language will offer their children better opportunities may stop speaking their mother tongue at home. Within a generation or two, the heritage language becomes something that grandparents use among themselves, and eventually not at all.
The loss matters for reasons that go beyond sentiment. Many endangered languages encode detailed knowledge about local plants, animals and landscapes, accumulated over centuries and often never written down. Some languages also organise ideas in ways that challenge assumptions linguists once held about how human language must work. Each language that disappears therefore narrows the evidence available for understanding the human mind.
Encouragingly, the decline is not always irreversible. Communities around the world have launched revitalisation programmes, ranging from immersion pre-schools to dictionaries compiled with the help of elderly speakers. Digital technology has added new tools: recordings, mobile apps and social media allow scattered speakers to hear and use their language daily. Revival is demanding, however. It depends less on outside experts than on whether younger members of the community come to see the language as a living part of their identity rather than a relic of the past.
